items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: we went to the Metropole one day and we sat there for eight hours listening to Coleman Hawkins

ctx.x: No it’s the guy that is a doctor. It’s an optician, isn’t it? Not an optometrist. Not the guy that makes the glasses, no, this is an optician. And as I’d say we’d go, and I was starting to get into listening to the bebop pretty good then. Although we would always go to Nick’s, we’d always go to Condon’s, we went to the Metropole one day and we sat there for eight hours listening to Coleman Hawkins and Charlie Shavers and Mickey Sheen was a great drummer then too. He’s since passed away. And I was in awe. And then…

I wanted to ask you a question, sort of rewind. You saw Charlie Shavers in the Dorsey band just down the street from here. Was there any — of course you were pretty young — but was there any significance to the fact that here’s this black man playing, who probably was the only black person in the band, right?
